newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court against Chinese couple's extradition.
newsitem.headline: Polish court against Chinese couple's extradition.

text.p: The Polish Supreme Court ruled on Friday that a Chinese couple, wanted by Beijing for alleged financial offences, would not be extradited from Poland because they would not get a fair trial in China.
"The court has ruled that an extradition (of the couple) would violate article three of the European Human Rights Convention," Judge Krzysztof Kauba, spokesman for the Supreme Court, told Reuters.
"In other words, it is possible that the trial in China would not meet European standards set by the human rights convention," he said. The Supreme Court's decision is final.
The ruling was welcomed by Polish human rights activists who had argued that if extradited, Mr Mandugeqi and his wife, Yinge, members of China's Mongolian minority, would risk a death penalty.
The couple have been held in Poland since last August on the basis of an Interpol warrant. Chinese authorities issued an arrest warrant in 1994, the year after they left the country.
The couple's lawyer Wojciech Hermelinski has said the pair faces allegations of fraud, failing to repay money borrowed from banks and individuals, together involving a sum of more than $1 million.
The couple has argued they repaid practically all they owed and that Beijing is pursuing them out of political motives.
The Chinese embassy issued a statement earlier this year saying the initial court decision preventing their extradition amounted to protection of criminals.
